title: The Human-Authored Textbook
author: Terry Underwood
summary: LLMs generate fluent text that resembles but lacks intentional pedagogical structure. Authored texts embody experienced judgments about foundations, misconceptions, and connections grounded in disciplinary knowledge and classroom observation. Synthetic text is consensus distilled, flattened of insight. Solution: not banning LLMs but training students to recognize differences and maintaining human authors as primary sources. Pre-reading, during-reading support, post-reading consolidation are legitimate LLM uses; substituting models undermines learning. Teachers remain final judges of what merits assignment.
points: Authored text reflects pedagogical intention grounded in lived experience; synthetic offers only statistical patterns.
Students must understand synthetic text has no accountability to subject matter or disciplinary community.
LLMs support periphery but cannot originate designed intellectual experience.
Five major textbook publishers resisted AI replacement of authors.
Students need explicit training in verification, comparison, and rhetorical judgment.
quotes: It is a human artifact shaped by pedagogical intention.
The cell is a human creation, a lens ground by a particular hand.
To read human-authored text for genuine learning is cooperative engagement.” “A student who grasps synthetic text will know when to consult models and return to authored sources.
We assigned intelligent to living beings and machines, obscuring fundamental difference.” Archived from Terry U Substack on April 21, 2026 by Tim.
